items.title: SightPress documentation
items.text:
SightPress is a powerful content management system (CMS) for everyone, designed with blind and low-vision creators and audiences in mind. It is built on modern, object-oriented PHP and is free software, licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later.

With SightPress you can run many websites from one installation, each in as many languages as you need. The admin area, the default theme and every built-in feature aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA. Every task works with a keyboard alone and with a screen reader.

items.title: Status
items.text: SightPress is in early development. There is no release yet, and these pages will grow as features are built.

items.title: Where to go next
items.text:
• The source code lives on GitHub in the SightPress organisation.
  • To run SightPress on your own computer, follow Getting started.
  • The how-to guides show you how to do one task at a time.

items.title: Getting started
items.text:
This guide shows you how to run SightPress on your own computer, so that you can try it out. You don't need to know how to program. It takes about 20 minutes, most of which is waiting for downloads.

What you can try today

SightPress is in early development. At this stage it starts up and shows a page that says no site is set up yet. You can't create a website yet. These guides will grow as features are built.

items.title: What you need
items.text:
• A computer running Windows 10 or 11, macOS, or Linux.
  • About 5 GB of free disk space.
  • An internet connection.
  • Permission to install programs on the computer.

You type some commands in a terminal. A terminal is a window where you type instructions instead of clicking:

  • On Windows, open Windows Terminal or PowerShell from the Start menu.
  • On macOS, open Terminal from Applications, then Utilities.
  • On Linux, open your terminal app.

Type or paste each command, then press Enter.

items.title: Step 1: install Docker
items.text:
Docker runs SightPress and everything it needs inside separate, self-contained boxes called containers. You don't have to install PHP, a web server or a database yourself.

  1. Install Docker:
    • On Windows or macOS, install Docker Desktop. On Windows, accept the option to use WSL 2 if the installer asks.
    • On Linux, install Docker Engine and the Docker Compose plugin.
  2. On Windows or macOS, open Docker Desktop and wait until it says that Docker is running.

  3. In the terminal, type:

    docker compose version

    You should see a line such as Docker Compose version v5.3.0. The number may be different. If you see "command not found" or a similar message, Docker is not installed correctly, or Docker Desktop is not running.

items.title: Step 2: install Git
items.text:
Git downloads the SightPress files from GitHub, where they are published.

  1. Install Git from the Git downloads page. On macOS, you can instead type git --version in the terminal and accept the offer to install the developer tools.

  2. In the terminal, type:

    git --version

    You should see a line such as git version 2.51.0.

items.title: Step 3: download SightPress
items.text:
SightPress comes in three parts, which must sit side by side in the same folder:

  • skeleton, the project you start;
  • core, which holds the features;

  • module-interface, which describes how add-ons talk to SightPress.

  • Make a folder for SightPress and go into it:

    mkdir sightpress
cd sightpress

  • Download the three parts:

    git clone https://github.com/sightpress/skeleton.git
git clone https://github.com/sightpress/core.git
git clone https://github.com/sightpress/module-interface.git

    After each command, you should see a few lines that end with done.

  • Go into the skeleton folder:

    cd skeleton

Only on Linux

The SightPress container writes files as user number 1000. If your Linux user has a different number, files can end up owned by the wrong user. Type id -u. If it shows anything other than 1000, copy the settings file with cp .env.example .env, open .env in a text editor, and set UID and GID to the numbers that id -u and id -g show. Windows and macOS users can skip this.

items.title: Step 4: start SightPress
items.text:
1. In the skeleton folder, type:

    docker compose up

  2. Wait. The first time, Docker downloads and builds everything it needs. This can take 5 to 15 minutes. You see many lines of text scroll past. Later starts take a few seconds.

  3. SightPress is ready when the text stops scrolling and you see lines starting with php-1 that end with ready to handle connections.

Leave this terminal window open. SightPress stops when you close it.

items.title: Step 5: open SightPress in your browser
items.text:
1. Open your web browser and go to http://localhost:8080.
  2. You should see a plain page with the heading No site configured and this text: "SightPress is running, but no site is set up for this address yet. If you look after this server, create a site and link this address to it." The browser tab is called "No site configured - SightPress".

This is the right result. It means SightPress is running. Every address shows this page until you create a site, which a later version will let you do.

The page follows your computer's light or dark setting. It has one heading and one main area, so a screen reader can find the message straight away.

If the browser shows 502 Bad Gateway, SightPress is still finishing its first start. Wait a minute, then reload the page.

items.title: Step 6: stop SightPress
items.text:
1. Go back to the terminal window where SightPress is running.
  2. Press Ctrl+C. You should see lines that end with Stopped.

To start SightPress again later, go to the skeleton folder and type docker compose up again.

items.title: If something goes wrong
items.text: "port is already allocated" or "address already in use" Another program on your computer is using one of the ports SightPress needs. See Change the ports SightPress uses. "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon" Docker is not running. On Windows or macOS, open Docker Desktop and wait until it says that Docker is running. On Linux, type sudo systemctl start docker. The page doesn't load at all Check that the terminal still shows SightPress running, and that the address is exactly http://localhost:8080, with http, not https.

items.title: What to do next
items.text: The how-to guides show you how to run SightPress in the background, start a database, open the test e-mail inbox and file storage, and try the command line tool.

items.title: How-to guides
items.text: Each guide shows you how to do one thing with SightPress, in short, numbered steps. They assume you have already followed Getting started, so SightPress is downloaded and runs on your computer.

items.title: Running SightPress
items.text:
• Run SightPress in the background, so that you can close the terminal.
  • Change the ports SightPress uses, if another program already uses them.
  • Start a database server: MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL.

items.title: Checking the built-in tools
items.text:
• Open the test e-mail inbox, which catches every e-mail SightPress sends.
  • Open the file storage console, where uploaded files will be kept.
  • Try the command line tool.

items.title: Coming later
items.text: SightPress is in early development. You can't create a website or put SightPress on a public server yet. Guides for those tasks will appear here when the features are ready.

items.title: Change the ports SightPress uses
items.text: A port is a numbered door on your computer that a program listens on. Each address SightPress uses ends in a port number, such as the 8080 in http://localhost:8080. If another program already uses one of these ports, SightPress can't start and you see an error such as "port is already allocated". This guide shows you how to choose different ports.

items.title: The ports SightPress uses
items.text:
Setting Default What it is for HTTP_PORT 8080 SightPress itself MAILPIT_UI_PORT 8025 The test e-mail inbox MAILPIT_SMTP_PORT 1025 Where the test e-mail inbox receives e-mail MINIO_API_PORT 9000 File storage MINIO_CONSOLE_PORT 9001 The file storage console

The error message names the port that is taken, for example 127.0.0.1:8080.

items.title: Change a port
items.text:
1. If SightPress is running, stop it. See Run SightPress in the background, or press Ctrl+C in the terminal where it runs.

  2. In the skeleton folder, check whether a file called .env exists. If it doesn't, create it by copying the example file:

    cp .env.example .env

    On Windows in PowerShell, cp works too.

  3. Open .env in a text editor, such as Notepad on Windows or TextEdit on macOS. The name starts with a dot, so some file browsers hide it; you can open it from the editor's Open menu instead.

  4. Find the line for the port you want to change, for example HTTP_PORT=8080, and change the number, for example to HTTP_PORT=8081. Pick a number between 1024 and 65535 that no other program uses.
  5. Save the file.
  6. Start SightPress again with docker compose up.
  7. Use the new number in the address. With HTTP_PORT=8081, go to http://localhost:8081. You should see the No site configured page.

items.title: Who can reach these ports
items.text: Every port listens only on your own computer (the address 127.0.0.1, also called localhost). Other computers on your network can't reach SightPress.

items.title: Open the file storage console
items.text:
SightPress will keep uploaded files, such as images and documents, in file storage. On your computer this storage is provided by a program called MinIO, which has its own web console. This guide shows you how to sign in to it.

  1. Start SightPress (see Getting started).
  2. In your web browser, go to http://localhost:9001.
  3. You should see the MinIO sign-in page.
  4. Sign in with the user name sightpress and the password sightpress-secret.
  5. You should see the MinIO console. There are no files yet.

SightPress doesn't store any files yet. Later versions will store uploads here.

If you changed MINIO_ROOT_USER, MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD or MINIO_CONSOLE_PORT in your .env file, use your values instead. These settings only take effect the first time the storage starts.

items.title: Open the test e-mail inbox
items.text:
When SightPress runs on your computer, it never sends real e-mail. Every message goes to a test inbox called Mailpit instead, so you can read it without anything leaving your computer. This guide shows you how to open it.

  1. Start SightPress (see Getting started).
  2. In your web browser, go to http://localhost:8025.
  3. You should see the Mailpit inbox. It is empty for now, with a message saying there are no messages.

SightPress doesn't send any e-mail yet. Later versions will send e-mail, for example when someone is invited to edit a site, and those messages will appear here.

If you changed MAILPIT_UI_PORT in your .env file, use that number instead of 8025.

items.title: Run SightPress in the background
items.text: In Getting started, SightPress runs in a terminal window and stops when you close it. This guide shows you how to run it in the background instead.

items.title: Start SightPress
items.text:
1. Open a terminal and go to the skeleton folder, for example:

    cd sightpress/skeleton

  2. Type:

    docker compose up --detach --wait

  3. Wait until the command finishes. You should see one line per container (php, nginx, mailpit and minio), each ending with Healthy. You get your terminal back.

  4. Go to http://localhost:8080. You should see the No site configured page.

    The very first time, SightPress keeps installing for a minute or two after the command finishes, and the browser shows 502 Bad Gateway. Wait a minute, then reload the page.

You can now close the terminal. SightPress keeps running until you stop it or restart your computer.

items.title: See what is running
items.text:
Type:

docker compose ps

You should see a table with one row for each container. The STATUS column says Up and how long the container has been running.

items.title: Read the messages SightPress writes
items.text:
Type:

docker compose logs --follow

You see the messages from every container, and new ones as they arrive. Press Ctrl+C to stop reading. SightPress keeps running.

items.title: Stop SightPress
items.text:
Type:

docker compose --profile "*" down

You should see lines ending with Removed. The --profile "*" part also stops a database server if you started one. Your settings and stored files are kept for next time.

Shortcuts for macOS and Linux

If the make program is installed, you can type make up to start SightPress in the background and make down to stop it. Type make on its own to list every shortcut.

items.title: Start a database server
items.text:
SightPress keeps its data in a single file on disk (an SQLite database), so it doesn't need a separate database server. If you want to try one, SightPress can start MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL for you. This guide shows you how.

Not used yet

At this stage SightPress starts the database server but doesn't store anything in it. You can check that it runs. Later versions will let you use it for your sites.

items.title: Start SightPress with a database
items.text:
1. If SightPress is running, stop it with docker compose --profile "*" down.

  2. In the skeleton folder, type one of these commands:

    docker compose --profile mysql up

    For MariaDB, use --profile mariadb. For PostgreSQL, use --profile postgres.

  3. Wait until the text stops scrolling. The first time, Docker downloads the database, which can take a few minutes. You should see lines starting with mysql-1 (or mariadb-1, or postgres-1) among the others.

To start it in the background instead, add --detach --wait to the end of the command.

items.title: Check that the database runs
items.text:
1. Open a second terminal and go to the skeleton folder.

  2. Type:

    docker compose --profile "*" ps

  3. You should see a row for the database, such as mysql, with (healthy) in the STATUS column. If it says (health: starting), wait a few seconds and type the command again.

When you start SightPress without --profile, no database server runs, and this table has no database row.

items.title: The database settings
items.text:
The database is created with these values. You can change them in the .env file before the first start (see Change the ports SightPress uses for how to create and edit .env).

Setting Default What it is DB_NAME sightpress The name of the database DB_USER sightpress The user name DB_PASSWORD sightpress The user's password DB_ROOT_PASSWORD sightpress-root The administrator password (MySQL, MariaDB)

The database server can only be reached by the other SightPress containers, not from your computer or your network.

items.title: Stop the database
items.text: Type docker compose --profile "*" down. This stops SightPress and the database. The data in the database is kept for next time.

items.title: Try the command line tool
items.text: SightPress has a command line tool for tasks such as creating a site. This guide shows you how to run it and what it can do today.

items.title: List the commands
items.text:
1. Open a terminal and go to the skeleton folder.

  2. Type:

    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress list

  3. You should see a short list of commands, including list and site:create <name>.

items.title: Try to create a site
items.text:
1. Type:

    docker compose run --rm --no-deps php bin/sightpress site:create demo

  2. You should see this message:

    Can't create the site "demo" yet: sites are not available in this version of SightPress.

This is the expected result. Creating sites will work in a later version, and this guide will show you how.

Shortcut for macOS and Linux

If the make program is installed, make site-create NAME=demo does the same thing.
